properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js is the SHA-1/SHA-2 engine inside the ethers web3 toolchain; the application never calls it directly — the browser wallet / hardhat does the signing. Dependency inventory, changeable here (npm install).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 ECDSA is what signs every EVM/Core-chain transaction these dapps send, but the primitive lives inside ethers/ganache, not application code — signing happens in the browser wallet or the hardhat deployer. This is the shipped dependency surface; replacing it is an ethers/library upgrade, not an app change.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey (OpenSSL legacy single-round MD5 KDF) ships with the dev toolchain only; no application code derives keys with it. Weak practice inside the package, recorded as part of the dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Poly1305 MAC ships with the tweetnacl/@noble dependencies of the web3 toolchain; no application call site. Modern MAC, nothing to remediate beyond eventual library rotation.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency (bcrypt-pbkdf, transitive via sshpk/ethereum tooling) in 4 lockfiles. Ships the bcrypt-pbkdf KDF; no direct call site in application code. Confirm as dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Math.random() in live frontend code: fabricates mock dashboard data (staking-reward increment in user-stats.tsx, fake sold/remaining/raised stats and a random hex ID in creator-dashboard.tsx) and — the interesting one — page.tsx:25 gates the dashboard owner view with setIsOwner(Math.random() > 0.7), a coin flip standing in for a real access check. Not a CSPRNG; acceptable for mock stats but the owner gate is UI access control that should derive from an on-chain check.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge enters via webpack dev-server, which uses it with selfsigned to mint local HTTPS dev certificates; the application itself never performs RSA. Dev-only tooling, still part of what the build ships.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.4.2 declares secp256k1 ECDSA. This is the dependency inventory; actual on-chain signing goes through ethers/MetaMask with the same quantum-vulnerable secp256k1 — EVM's ECDSA is dictated by the blockchain protocol (observable here, replaceable only by the protocol/vendor). Migration when a consumer appears: ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency in package-lock.json (part of the wallet/ethers SDK tree, e.g. @coinbase/wallet-sdk). No direct X25519 call site in application code — presence is the dependency inventory. Changeable here by removing/upgrading the dependency; the classical key agreement it ships is retroactively breakable (migrate to X25519MLKEM768 when a consumer appears).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared dependency in package-lock.json (wallet/ethers SDK tree). No direct Ed25519 call site in application code. Classical signature primitive — deadline (not harvesting) risk; migration ML-DSA-65 when a consumer appears.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.4.2 declares Ed25519 in 02's lockfile. Dependency inventory; no direct Ed25519 call site in application code. Classical signature — deadline risk (Shor); migration ML-DSA-65 when a consumer appears.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is the browser-side secp256k1 ECDSA engine behind ethers; all actual signing happens in the user's injected wallet. Dependency inventory, changeable via ethers upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.4.2 declares P-256 (secp256r1) in 02's lockfile. Dependency inventory; no direct P-256 call site in application code. Classical curve — Shor-vulnerable (ECDSA/ECDH); hybrid X25519MLKEM768 / ML-DSA migration when a consumer appears.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic exposes ECDH as well as ECDSA; the dapp never performs a key agreement in app code. Recorded as part of the shipped dependency surface.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl enters via the ganache/hardhat toolchain; its X25519 box implementation ships in the dependency tree but is unused by the application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: keccak / @ethersproject/keccak256 / js-sha3 declared across the projects' package-lock.json files — the Ethereum toolchain ships Keccak-256 everywhere (EVM hashing). SHA-3 is PQ-safe (Grover only halves preimage resistance); no migration pressure. The two FIRST-PARTY Solidity keccak256 uses are separate findings (08-Guess-Game weak PRNG, 12-Core-MultiSig CREATE2 salt) because they are not part of this object's sites.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: pbkdf2 / @ethersproject/pbkdf2 / @types/pbkdf2 declared across projects' lockfiles (ethers uses PBKDF2 for keystore/wallet encryption with its own fixed parameters). No first-party PBKDF2 call site exists (grep for pbkdf2Sync/createHash in app code = 0 hits), so no CWE-916 iteration-count risk is reachable from this repository.

properties.name: pqs:context
